sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily on first access.
sketches.resonance: Declaring someone as an `object` means the language itself guarantees there will never be another; uniqueness is not a choice but an enforced constraint.

sketches.mechanism: A `weak` reference does not prevent deallocation — the referent can vanish at any time, leaving behind `nil`.
sketches.resonance: Holding someone weakly means your grip alone is not enough to keep them; they disappear the moment nothing stronger holds on.

sketches.mechanism: Wait — Haskell was used in last 10 days. Let me choose Go instead: a send on a closed channel causes a panic at runtime, an unrecoverable crash.
sketches.resonance: You closed the channel, but I kept trying to send — the language makes it fatal to speak into what has already ended.
